terms.p: The part of your code a diagnostic underlines with carets, marking where the compiler stopped. That is not always where the mistake is.
A place the compiler underlines with dashes because it participates in the error, such as the earlier borrow that made a later one illegal.
The stable identifier printed in square brackets after the word error, which you can look up with rustc --explain.
The official page listing every rustc error code with a minimal broken example and a fixed one, the same text rustc --explain prints.
You may only implement a trait for a type if you defined one of the two, so that no two crates can claim the same implementation.
